name: Aubrey Beardsley
bio: Artist (1872-98). He was working in an insurance office until 1892; his drawings were first published in February 1893, he illustrated the English Salomé, and he was art editor of the Yellow Book and then the Savoy before dying of tuberculosis at twenty-five. One letter from Wilde to him survives - an invitation to dinner at Kettner's with Robert Ross - but the warmer document is an inscription Wilde wrote in a copy of Salomé in March 1893: 'For Aubrey: for the only artist who, besides myself, knows what the dance of the seven veils is, and can see that invisible dance.'
bio_note: The letter is 'APPARENTLY THE ONLY SURVIVING LETTER FROM WILDE TO BEARDSLEY', undatable within six months. The General Index records a cooling - 'his dislike of W' (printed 919 n.) at Dieppe in 1897.
